title: A note on diffusive/random-walk behaviour in Metropolis--Hastings algorithms
summary: We prove a general result that if a Metropolis--Hastings algorithm has a proposal that is not geometrically ergodic and the acceptance rate approaches unity at a suitable rate as the state variable becomes large, then the Metropolised chain will also not be geometrically ergodic. Our conditions seem stronger than might be expected, but are shown to be necessary through a counterexample. We then turn our attention to the random walk and guided walk Metropolis algorithms.
